<a name="snap-hints"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Hints

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Hints
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Hints.php:30](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Hints.php#L30)

Class Hints
Snap Cards work without any hint: every card is built from what a capability declares (its rules, descriptions,
readOnly and destructive). Hints only make them better, from one file the app owns, application/config/snap.php:

```
return [
    'about' => 'a library app',                       // what the assistant is the assistant of (the planner)
    'cards' => [                                      // keyed by capability name
        'list_books' => ['title' => 'The catalog', 'columns' => ['title', 'author.name'], 'empty' => 'No book yet.'],
        'reading_report' => ['async' => true, 'working' => ['Counting the books…']],
    ],
];
```

A file that returns the cards alone (no 'cards' key) works too. The keys of a card are in the wiki page
"Snap Cards and the Assistant": title, lead, submit, columns, labels, hide, values, choices, open, full, empty,
variant, noun, icon, done, undo, next, applies, empty_next, alert, insight, discover, working, async, consequence,
confirm, card (2.25.0: its card view, 'Folder/view' under application/views, or false), view (2.24.0: the page whose
part marked data-snap shows it, or false) and design (2.24.0: how its data is shown without a card view or a page).
A capability is async when #[Capability(async: true)] says so, or its hint does.

<a name="snap-views"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Views

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Views
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Views.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Views.php#L25)

Class Views
How a Show card looks, best first (2.25.0):
1. its card view: application/views/snap/&lt;capability&gt;.pug, a Pug view made for the card, in the app's own markup and classes, rendered on the server into the card (the hint 'card' =&gt; 'Folder/view' names another, false none). It gets $result (what the capability returned), $rows and $page for a list, $record for one record, $input, $card, $home, $authorized and $user. A link with data-snap-open="&lt;capability&gt;" and data-snap-input='{"id":7}' opens that card in the conversation. Written by Claude from the app's views (the assistant skill); its first line names the page it was made from and that page's fingerprint, so `php caligrafer.php snap views` says when it is stale.
2. the part of its page marked data-snap="&lt;capability&gt;" (a Route::page whose first data it is), embedded in the card (?snap-embed: no frame, sized to it); a whole page only when the hint 'view' names it
3. a card designed for its data in the app's design system (Snap\Designer)

<a name="snap-designer"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Designer

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Designer
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Designer.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Designer.php#L23)

Class Designer
A capability shown through its own page uses that page (Snap\Views). Without one, its card is designed, never dumped:
a design says which of the data makes the title, the line under it, the badges, the numbers that stand out, the
details, the longer text and the tags of a record, or the title, line, details and badge of each row of a list.
The page then draws it with the app's own design tokens (its DESIGN_STYLE), so it looks like the rest of the app.

Who designs it: the hint 'design' of application/config/snap.php when the app gives one; else Claude (when the
assistant has its key), once for each shape of data, kept in the cache; else rules from the names of the fields.

### Constants

+ `FORMATS = array('text', 'number', 'money', 'percent', 'date', 'datetime', 'bool', 'email', 'url')`
+ `TONES = array('success', 'warning', 'danger', 'info', 'neutral')`
+ `CACHE_DAYS = 30`

### Public properties

+ `public static $model = true`: bool false: rules only, never the model (tests, and a design asked for while answering)
+ `public static $transport = null`: Tests fake Claude's design here (a callable that takes the request and returns the response), apart from the planner's: a test that fakes the planner never sees the designer's requests

### Methods

+ [`Designer::record()`](#snap-designer-record)
+ [`Designer::rows()`](#snap-designer-rows)
+ [`Designer::spec()`](#snap-designer-spec)
+ [`Designer::paths()`](#snap-designer-paths)
+ [`Designer::format()`](#snap-designer-format)

<a name="snap-planner"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Planner

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Planner
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Planner.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Planner.php#L25)

The Snap shell's planner (2.23.0): Claude reads what the person typed or said and answers with cards.

What the model may do, enforced here, not in the prompt:

- look things up with the read-only capabilities this person may call (as tools, run with their permissions);
- answer with show_cards: which capability, with which values, and one sentence of caption.

Every card it names goes through Snap\Flow like any other: a read runs, a change comes back as an Ask: Confirm
whose token only the person's click sends. The model never sees a token and never runs a change.
Tool results are the app's data: the system prompt says so, and nothing in them can reach a change anyway.

Claude through the official PHP SDK (anthropic-ai/sdk), claude-opus-5-5 at low effort (a quick turn in a UI),
server-side refusal fallbacks on. Without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the planner is off and the shell uses its fast path.

### Constants

+ `MODEL = 'claude-opus-5-5'`
+ `MAX_STEPS = 6`
+ `RESULT_BYTES = 12000`
+ `FILE_TYPES = array('image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf', 'text/plain', 'text/csv', 'text/markdown')`
+ `FILE_BYTES = 5242880`
+ `FILES = 3`

### Public properties

+ `public static $transport = null`: callable|null tests: fn (array $request): object  (a response with -&gt;stopReason and -&gt;content)

### Methods

+ [`Planner::on()`](#snap-planner-on)
+ [`Planner::files()`](#snap-planner-files)
+ [`Planner::plan()`](#snap-planner-plan)
+ [`Planner::send()`](#snap-planner-send)

<a name="snap-flow"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Flow

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Flow
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Flow.php:16](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Flow.php#L16)

The next card for a capability and its inputs, the same whoever asks (a card that is sent, the shell's fast path,
the model's choice): one place decides, so the planner can never take a shortcut around consent.

```
read:        inputs missing -> its Ask card; complete -> runs -> Show card
write/destroy: inputs missing -> its Ask card; refused by its rules -> Ask with errors; else -> Ask: Confirm
```

A change runs only in SnapRun, with the token of that Confirm.

### Methods

+ [`Flow::next()`](#snap-flow-next)
+ [`Flow::refused()`](#snap-flow-refused)

<a name="snap-consent"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Consent

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Consent
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Consent.php:20](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Consent.php#L20)

Snap consent (2.23.0): nothing that changes data runs from a card until the person confirms it.

- snap_run answers a change with an Ask: Confirm: what will change (before -&gt; after), and a one-time token bound to this person, this capability and these exact inputs, for 10 minutes, kept in the session (never in the card's address). Only the person's click on that card sends it back; a model, a page or a link cannot make one.
- A confirmed change is recorded in Caligrafy's audit log (capability snap_confirm, detail: what was confirmed).
- What the change can be undone with is decided here, from what was true before (update_), what was created (create_ -&gt; delete_), or a hint ('undo' in application/config/snap.php). Undoing is a change too: it gets its own Confirm.

### Constants

+ `TTL = 600`
+ `KEEP = 20`
+ `KEY = 'snap_consent'`

### Methods

+ [`Consent::ask()`](#snap-consent-ask)

+ [`Consent::undo()`](#snap-consent-undo)

<a name="snap-offers"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Offers

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Offers
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Offers.php:26](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Offers.php#L26)

Offer: Suggestion and Offer: Routine (2.23.0): the assistant notices what a person does again and again,
only if they turned noticing on, and offers to help. Built to stay quiet rather than noisy:

- opt-in per person (snap_settings.noticing), off by default; "What I've noticed" shows every pattern, each deletable, and turning noticing off deletes what was noticed
- a pattern is the same request (capability + inputs) on 3 different days or more, on the same weekday (weekly) or around the same hour (daily); anything weaker says nothing
- every offer says why ("you did this 4 Mondays in a row"), has Not now and Don't suggest this again, and at most MAX_OFFERS are shown at a time
- Offer: Suggestion: it is the usual moment and it was not done yet today: do it now (through Snap\Flow, so a change still asks for its Confirm)
- Offer: Routine: do it on that rhythm, at a level the person picks: suggest (a Suggestion at that moment), confirm (its Confirm ready at that moment), auto (it runs as a task and they are told). Accepting a routine is itself a change with its Ask: Confirm. A delete is never automatic.

### Constants

+ `MIN_DAYS = 3`
+ `MAX_OFFERS = 2`
+ `WINDOW_DAYS = 42`
+ `LEVELS = array('suggest', 'confirm', 'auto')`
+ `DAYS = array(1 => 'Monday', 2 => 'Tuesday', 3 => 'Wednesday', 4 => 'Thursday', 5 => 'Friday', 6 => 'Saturday', 7 => 'Sunday')`

### Public properties

<a name="snap-tasks"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Tasks

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Tasks
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Tasks.php:24](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Tasks.php#L24)

Track: Task cards (2.23.0): work that runs in the background for one person.

A capability declared #[Capability(async: true)] (or with the hint 'async' in application/config/snap.php) does not run
in the request: a read starts as a task at once, a change after its Ask: Confirm. The task is a row of snap_tasks and
a job of Caligrafy's queue (snap_task_run). The worker runs the capability AS THE PERSON who asked (their user, the
web channel: their permissions, not the queue's full access), keeps the card of what came out, and notifies them:

```
done        -> the Show card of the result
needs_input -> the Ask card of what the capability refused (the person answers it, a new task starts)
failed      -> a notice, after the queue's retries
```

The Track card shows where it is: queued, running, then the card it ended with.

+ `TABLE = 'caligrafy_snap_tasks'`

<a name="snap-discover"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Discover

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Discover
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Discover.php:28](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Discover.php#L28)

Discover (2.23.0): Home surfaces the things this application is about, to
invite browsing, the way a shop surfaces products. Out of the box, from one hint on a list capability ('discover'):

- for you      more like what this person looked at (only when they turned noticing on: what they opened is in snap_events), e.g. another book by the author of a book they opened
- new          what was added last
- the rule     a business rule of the app: only what is available now (not in another list, e.g. not lent)

Each pick is a Home card that opens the object in the task space; each says why it is there.

The hint: 'discover' =&gt; array(

```
'open' => 'get_book', 'key' => 'id',                     how an object opens (capability, the field it takes)
'title' => 'title', 'meta' => array('author.name', ...),   what a pick shows
'new' => 'created_at',                                   the field that says when it was added
'related' => 'author.id', 'by' => 'author.name',          what "more like it" shares, and its name
'opened' => array('get_book' => 'id', 'lend_book' => 'book_id'),   the requests that mean "looked at it"
'unavailable' => array('capability' => 'list_loans', 'field' => 'book_id'),   the business rule
'title_section' => 'On the shelf for you')
```

+ `PICKS = 6`

<a name="snap-shell"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Snap\Shell

```php
namespace Caligrafy\Snap;

class Shell
```

Source: [framework/core/Snap/Shell.php:15](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Snap/Shell.php#L15)

The Snap shell's fast path (2.23.0): what it can answer without a model, at once and for free:

- "What can I do?" (help, menu, ?): the cards this person may use, by family
- the title of one of their shortcuts: that Go: Shortcut, run
- the title or the name of a card ("the catalog", "lend a book", "list_loans"): that card

Anything else goes to the planner (Claude) when it is on.

<a name="snap-shell-onfocus"></a>
#### `Shell::onFocus()`

```php
public static function onFocus($text, Context $context, $focus)
```

A follow-up on the record the conversation is about, at once: "delete it", "change this", "lend that one".
Anything longer ("lend it to Sam") goes to the planner, with the conversation's memory.

**Parameters**

+ `$text`
+ `$context` `Context`
+ `$focus` `array|null`: ['capability' =&gt; 'get_book', 'input' =&gt; ['id' =&gt; 7]]
